dedupe_keys.name: sebago lake watershed maine economic case for a water and forest conservation fund daigneault and strong 2018

description: This case study makes the economic case for a fund to conserve forests in the 282,000-acre Sebago Lake watershed, which gives drinking water to more than 200,000 people around Portland, Maine, under one of about 50 US filtration exemptions. Adam Daigneault of the University of Maine and Aaron Strong of Hamilton College prepared it for the Sebago Clean Waters partnership in November 2018. Using the InVEST model, land use change scenarios, economic valuation and benefit-cost analysis, they estimate forest ecosystem services at USD 42 to 287 million a year, and find that if development forced the Portland Water District to build a USD 150 million filtration plant, rates would rise about 84%, adding over USD 1.7 million a year for the ten largest users. With only 10% of the watershed protected and forest cover down 3.5% from 1987 to 2009, protection is cheaper for commercial users than those charges. Coverage is the Sebago Lake watershed. Format and access: a 79-page PDF report. Licence: not stated; free. Caveats: values depend on scenario assumptions. It supports investment appraisal of forests as natural water infrastructure. Related catalogue records are InVEST and the Rio Camboriú watershed ROI study.
